reason: While Nabal, a wealthy landowner, is portrayed extremely unfavorably (described as harsh, evil-minded, a 'fool,' a 'son of Belial,' and ultimately struck dead by God), other elite figures in this passage are portrayed positively. David, an important military figure and future king, is depicted favorably as righteous, discerning, and favored by God. Abigail, though connected to the elite through marriage to Nabal, is portrayed very favorably as wise, understanding, beautiful, and virtuous. The text does not uniformly portray elite people unfavorably; rather, it contrasts the corrupt Nabal with the virtuous Abigail and the honorable David.
